goal: Translate long-term CLONEID lineage paths into tractable PhysiCell model phases without simulating raw calendar time minute-by-minute.

strategies.title: Primary-Lineage Interval Phases
strategies.phase_definition: Each adjacent primary-lineage interval Event_i -> Event_i+1 along passaged_from_id1 is one phase.

event_to_physicell_mapping.initial_conditions: First Event on the lineage path initializes the simulation.
event_to_physicell_mapping.event_schedule: Each subsequent Event closes one phase and starts the next.
event_to_physicell_mapping.bottlenecks_passaging: Passage or reseeding transitions are explicit transfer/bottleneck events between phases.
event_to_physicell_mapping.harvest_endpoints: Harvest-labeled Events serve as validation checkpoints or final endpoints.
event_to_physicell_mapping.perspective_constraints: Perspective.origin records attached to terminal Events provide endpoint molecular constraints.
event_to_physicell_mapping.identity_support: Identity is retained only as inferred secondary support.

model_family_meaning.neutral_growth: All phases share the same intrinsic rules; only schedule and bottlenecks differ.
model_family_meaning.fixed_state_fitness: 2N and 4N branches differ by stable effective fitness across phases.
model_family_meaning.density_dependent_or_resource_sensitive_: Branch differences emerge through context-sensitive crowding or resource response during each phase.

comparison_tests: 2N versus 4N branch differences under related O2-labeled lineage history
whether bottleneck structure alone explains divergence
whether density/resource dependence improves fit over neutral growth
assumptions: Each primary-lineage interval is a meaningful biological episode.
Phase normalization does not destroy the signal of interest.
Passage transitions matter more than literal waiting time.
failure_modes: Equal simulated duration may over-compress some intervals and under-compress others.
Some intervals may still represent heterogeneous biology.
Passaging effects may be confounded with media or oxygen history.

strategies.title: Seed-to-Harvest Episode Phases
strategies.phase_definition: A phase is a bounded seed-to-harvest or seed-to-next-transfer experimental episode, potentially spanning multiple adjacent Events.

event_to_physicell_mapping.event_schedule: Intermediate Events inside an episode become internal checkpoints.
event_to_physicell_mapping.bottlenecks_passaging: Harvest-to-reseed transitions become hard resets between phases.
event_to_physicell_mapping.harvest_endpoints: Harvest Events are the main phase endpoints.
event_to_physicell_mapping.perspective_constraints: Terminal Perspective records constrain episode endpoints.

model_family_meaning.neutral_growth: Episodes share one biological program, separated by reseeding or bottlenecks.
model_family_meaning.fixed_state_fitness: Branch-specific fitness is stable across repeated episodes.
model_family_meaning.density_dependent_or_resource_sensitive_: Episode-level environment dependence explains divergence within seeded culture periods.

comparison_tests: whether branch differences are stable across repeated seed-to-harvest episodes
whether bottleneck handling plus density/resource sensitivity is sufficient
assumptions: Seed-to-harvest episodes are the right biological unit.
Grouped Events within an episode are coherent under one local model context.
failure_modes: Grouping may hide informative Event-to-Event variation.

strategies.title: Regime-Bounded Phases
strategies.phase_definition: A phase is defined by stable media, stressor, oxygen-labeled, or local flask/seeding regime context.

event_to_physicell_mapping.initial_conditions: First Event in a regime initializes that phase.
event_to_physicell_mapping.event_schedule: Events inside a regime become trajectory checkpoints.
event_to_physicell_mapping.bottlenecks_passaging: Regime changes are explicit schedule changes.
event_to_physicell_mapping.perspective_constraints: Perspective.origin records provide endpoint molecular support.

model_family_meaning.neutral_growth: One biological program persists across context shifts.
model_family_meaning.fixed_state_fitness: Intrinsic branch differences persist across regimes.
model_family_meaning.density_dependent_or_resource_sensitive_: Context switches directly modulate effective growth behavior.

comparison_tests: media/regime dependence versus stable intrinsic lineage-state differences
assumptions: Regime labels capture the dominant selective context.
Grouping by regime does not collapse too much lineage detail.
failure_modes: This strategy may over-interpret context labels as mechanisms.

recommended_default_strategy.reason: Closest to the explicit lineage graph, preserves provenance cleanly, and requires the fewest extra biological assumptions.

backup_strategy.reason: Useful if interval-level phases are too fine-grained or if episode boundaries are already clear in the lineage records.

open_questions_for_user: Should the first biological proof-of-principle comparison prioritize 4N/O2 vs 2N/O2, 4N/O2 vs 4N/O1, or a three-branch comparison?
Should the first manuscript figure emphasize intrinsic 2N vs 4N differences, oxygen/regime adaptation, or both?
For first implementation, should phase duration stay fixed per lineage interval, fixed per seed-to-harvest episode, or scaled by phenotype change magnitude?
Should the first biological proof-of-principle use only cellCount, cellCount plus correctedCount, or cellCount plus correctedCount plus areaOccupied_um2 as joint calibration targets?
